name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
principle: Code writes past the bounds of a buffer allocated on the stack, usually a local fixed-size array. This can corrupt adjacent stack data such as saved frame pointers and return addresses, causing crashes or arbitrary code execution.
detection_signals: local fixed-size array char buf[N] written by strcpy(buf, src)
local fixed-size array char buf[N] written by strcat(buf, src)
local fixed-size array char buf[N] written by sprintf(buf, fmt, ...) or vsprintf(buf, fmt, ...)
gets(buf) where buf is a local stack array
scanf("%s", buf) or fscanf(...,"%s",buf) with no field width and buf is a local stack array
loop writes buf[i++] = input[j++] without i < sizeof(buf) guard
strcpy(hostname, hp->h_name) or similar library-returned string copied into local fixed-size array
negative_signals: destination buffer allocated with malloc/new, not a local stack array
copy length checked as strlen(src) < sizeof(buf) before copying into local array
snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s", src) used and return value/truncation handled
scanf format contains width less than destination capacity, e.g. scanf("%255s", buf) for char buf[256]
loop condition enforces i < sizeof(buf)-1 and writes terminating '\0'
false_defense_traps: strncpy(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) without guaranteed NUL termination
strncat(dst, src, sizeof(dst)) using total buffer size instead of remaining capacity
relying only on stack canaries, /GS, FORTIFY_SOURCE, ASLR, PIE, or DEP/NX
validating input format but not validating copied output length, e.g. hostname after gethostbyaddr
verification_focus: Does any write into a stack-allocated fixed-size buffer allow more bytes than the destination capacity including the NUL terminator?

consequence_chains.trigger: overflow corrupts saved frame pointer, stack pointer, or control data

patch_principle: Remove unbounded APIs such as gets, strcpy, strcat, sprintf, and widthless scanf for stack buffers.
Check source length against sizeof(destination) before copying, including space for the NUL terminator.
Use bounded formatting/copying APIs with the destination capacity and handle truncation explicitly.
Prefer safer abstractions such as std::string, std::array with checked access, or vetted wrapper functions.
Enable compiler/runtime hardening such as /GS, FORTIFY_SOURCE, stack canaries, ASLR, PIE, and DEP/NX as defense in depth only.
